'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Civilian casualties in the war in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
***According to [[Save the Children]], over 26,000 children have been killed in the [[Afghanistan]] war from 2005 to 2019. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-55039535?via=webuproar (BBC News)]
*[[Second Saudi–Yemeni War]], [[Iran–Saudi Arabia proxy conflict]]
**The [[Iran]]ian-backed [[Houthi movement|Houthis]] say they attacked a [[Saudi Aramco]] [[oil terminal]] in [[Jeddah]] with a new type of [[Quds 1|Quds cruise missile]]. [[Saudi Arabia]] acknowledges the attack. [https://apnews.com/article/dubai-united-arab-emirates-media-summits-g-20-summit-d69e8ebca362fa1b89c60887016ab178 (AP)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
*****[[California]] reports 20,654 new cases in the last 24 hours, a new single-day record since the pandemic began. [https://www.sfchronicle.com/bayarea/article/California-records-more-than-20-000-new-cases-15749853.php (''San Francisco Chronicle'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio]]
*****[[Ohio]] reports a new single-day record of 11,885 new cases. This number is likely inflated because of a two-day backlog from multiple labs. [https://www.dispatch.com/story/news/2020/11/23/dewine-ohio-hospital-leaders-provide-covid-19-update-monday/6389938002/ (''The Columbus Dispatch'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maryland]]
*****[[Maryland]] is expected to send state troopers to enforce restrictions in the state for [[Thanksgiving]]. [https://www.nbcwashington.com/news/coronavirus/coronavirus-in-maryland/maryland-troopers-to-help-with-pandemic-related-compliance-efforts/2485482/ (WRC-TV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Manitoba]]
*****[[Manitoba]] reports a record 540 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the total confirmed cases to 13,087 and pushing the five-day positivity rate tests to 14%. [https://winnipeg.ctvnews.ca/manitoba-reports-record-spike-of-more-than-540-new-covid-19-cases-on-monday-1.5200583 (CKY-DT)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario]]
*****[[Ontario]] reports 1,589 new cases, a new single-day record. [https://globalnews.ca/news/7478655/ontario-coronavirus-cases-november-23-covid19/ (Global News)]
****Nationwide, a record 5,713 new cases reported in [[Canada]] in the last 24 hours, bringing the nationwide confirmed cases to 337,555. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/coronavirus-covid19-canada-world-november-23-1.5812272 (CBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in England]]
*****[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] announces that gyms, bars, and non-essential shops across [[England]] will be allowed to reopen when the lockdown ends on December 2. The [[Second COVID-19 tier regulations in England|three-tiered regional measures]] will return at the same time, but with tighter rules. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-55048990 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] surpasses 50,000 total deaths from COVID-19. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/coronavirus-italy-death-toll-tops-50000/ (CBS News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a new single-day record of 25,173 cases, bringing the nationwide total since the beginning of the pandemic to 2.11 million cases. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/russia-reports-record-25-173-daily-covid-19-cases/2052824 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[King of Spain|King]] [[Felipe VI]] voluntarily quarantines for 10 days after being in close contact with someone who later tested positive for COVID-19. [https://www.euroweeklynews.com/2020/11/23/spains-king-in-10-days-quarantine-after-contact-tests-positive-for-coronavirus/ (Euro weekly News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] reports a record 6,713 new cases and 153 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide totals to 453,535 confirmed cases and 12,511 deaths. [https://www.dailysabah.com/turkey/turkeys-covid-19-death-toll-rises-by-153-in-last-24-hours/news (''Daily Sabah'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Selangor]]
*****The [[Government of Malaysia|government]] announces that it will temporarily close 28 [[Top Glove]] factories in [[Klang (city)|Klang]] in stages to enable the [[Minister of Health (Malaysia)|Health Ministry]] to conduct COVID-19 screening and quarantine workers. This comes as the world's largest surgical glove maker sees an increase in infections among factory workers. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20201123-world-s-top-surgical-glove-maker-shuts-factories-due-to-coronavirus (France 24)]
****The number of new confirmed cases in [[Malaysia]] increases by a record 1,884 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of cases to 56,659. 1,203 of these cases are from [[Selangor]] due to an increase in new infections in workplaces in the [[Klang Valley]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/covid-19-malaysia-record-1884-cases-spike-workplace-top-glove-13622006 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] surpasses 500,000 total confirmed cases of COVID-19. [https://kabar24.bisnis.com/read/20201123/15/1321374/covid-19-tembus-500000-sebulan-lebih-cepat-dari-ramalan-erick-thohir (Bisnis.com)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]]'s [[Cabinet of Thailand|Cabinet]] extends a COVID-19 [[state of emergency]] for 45 days until January 15, 2021. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2024171/state-of-emergency-extended-to-jan-15 (''The Bangkok Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***The land border between [[New South Wales]] and [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] reopens after 137 days of closure. People will now be able to travel between the two states without permits. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-11-22/nsw-coronavirus-gladys-berejiklian-marks-vic-border-reopening/12903540 (ABC Australia)]
***Victoria eases restrictions, allowing larger public and private gatherings, larger capacity quotas for businesses, and relaxing of the mask mandate so that masks will only be required in settings where social distancing is impractical. Chief Health Officer Brett Sutton states that he is confident there will be no community transmission in the state. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-11-22/victoria-daniel-andrews-on-coronavirus-restrictions-changes/12907456 (ABC Australia)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[AstraZeneca]] and [[University of Oxford]]'s vaccine showed 90% efficacy when it was given to 2,741 people as a half-dose followed by a full dose and 62% efficacy when two full doses were given to 8,895 people. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/11/23/europe/astrazeneca-oxford-coronavirus-vaccine-intl/index.html (CNN)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Israel–Saudi Arabia relations]]
**[[Israel]]i media reports that, on Sunday, [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] secretly flew to [[Neom]] in [[Saudi Arabia]] for a meeting with Crown Prince [[Mohammed bin Salman]]. [[Alternate Prime Minister of Israel|Alternate Prime Minister]] [[Benny Gantz]] describes "the leak of the prime minister's secret flight to Saudi Arabia" as "an irresponsible move". Saudi Arabia denies that such a meeting occurred. On Saturday, [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Saudi Arabia)|Saudi Foreign Minister]] [[Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud]] repeated the 2002 Saudi [[Arab Peace Initiative]] offer to fully normalize relations, only after the [[Palestinians]] achieve statehood. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-55042055 (BBC News)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/11/23/world/middleeast/israel-saudi-netanyahu-visit.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Corruption in France]]
**The first trial of former [[President of France|President]] [[Nicolas Sarkozy]], on charges of corruption and influence peddling in 2014, starts. [https://abcnews.go.com/Business/wireStory/french-president-sarkozy-stands-trial-corruption-74356391 (ABC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2020 United States presidential election]], [[Presidential transition of Joe Biden]]
**The [[General Services Administration]] officially certifies [[President-elect of the United States|President-elect]] [[Joe Biden]] as the "apparent winner" of the 2020 presidential election, and announces that the formal transition will be allowed to begin. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/11/23/politics/transition-biden-gsa-begin/index.html (CNN)] [https://apnews.com/article/joe-biden-health-national-security-rob-portman-coronavirus-pandemic-ac923137dfb664e5c3a1923f52eebbad (AP)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Chinese Lunar Exploration Program]]
**The [[China National Space Administration]] successfully launches the [[Chang'e 5]] robotic spacecraft from the [[Wenchang Spacecraft Launch Site]]. It is China's first [[sample return mission]], and if the mission is successful it will be the first lunar sample return mission since the [[Soviet Union]]'s ''[[Luna 24]]'' in 1976. Chang'e-5 will bring back at least 2 kilograms of [[Regolith|lunar soil]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/nov/23/china-launches-change-5-mission-to-bring-back-rocks-from-moon (''The Guardian'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]]
**[[2020 NFL season]]
***The [[National Football League]] extends their mask mandate and threatens to discipline anybody who violates the league's COVID-19 protocols. [https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/breaking/ct-nfl-masks-fines-covid-19-20201124-ksfow5l7szg57kujbs6asmgmlu-story.html (''Chicago Tribune'')] 
*[[FIFA]] bans the [[List of presidents of CAF|president]] of the [[Confederation of African Football]] [[Ahmad Ahmad]] from all [[Association football|football]]-related activity for five years, following an investigation into financial misconduct. He is also fined $220,000. Ahmad declined to comment on the ban. [https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2020/11/23/african-football-head-ahmad-banned-for-five-years-by-fifa (Al Jazeera)]
